name: Zerubbabel (son of Shealtiel/Pedaiah)
title: Leader of the people of Judah and rebuilder of the temple
summary: Zerubbabel was a descendant of King David who led the first group of Jewish exiles back from Babylon to Jerusalem. He played a crucial role in rebuilding the temple and was a messianic forerunner figure who gave hope for the restoration of David's kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Leader of the Exiles Returning from Babylon
keyEvents.description: Zerubbabel led the first large group of Jewish exiles back to Judah after Cyrus's decree, along with the high priest Joshua (Jeshua).

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding the Altar and Laying the Temple Foundation
keyEvents.description: Zerubbabel and Joshua rebuilt the altar and laid the foundation for the new temple, which brought great joy among the people.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to Temple Construction
keyEvents.description: Work on the temple was halted due to opposition from the local population and political interference, remaining stopped for many years.

keyEvents.title: The Prophet Haggai Encourages Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: Through the prophet Haggai, God spoke to Zerubbabel and urged him to complete the temple, promising His presence and blessing.

keyEvents.title: Zerubbabel as God's Signet Ring
keyEvents.description: God declared through Haggai that Zerubbabel was chosen as His signet ring, a messianic title pointing to the line of David and future salvation.

keyEvents.title: The Temple Completed
keyEvents.description: Under Zerubbabel's leadership, the second temple was completed and dedicated, about 70 years after the first temple was destroyed.
